rows.label: Baseline rates of European migration in child's network (Best-guess)
rows.explainer: I base this estimate on two statistics: the emigrant-to-home population ratio in Uganda (5%), and the percentage of migrating Africans who migrate to Europe (18% ~= 20%) For emigrant-to-home population ratio in Uganda, see Map 1.1 (page 45) in World Bank (2018). From the Economist: "Only 18% of those (Africans) living abroad are in Europe. About 70% are in other African countries", The Economist (2021)

rows.label: Income for those who migrate net of remittances & repayments (Best-guess)
rows.explainer: My best-guess takes the mid-point of starting salaries for engineering, agriculture, and English graduates, which I think are representative of the types of degrees Malengo students would study. From the resulting figure ($44k), I subtract $4k to account for remittances. I don't subtract the $30k repayment amount because: i) over the course of a 40 year life, $30k ~= $1k per year; ii) this parameter is pretty uncertain to begin with; iii) the bottom-line actually isn't that sensitive to this parameter (b/c of our logarithmic utility assumption)

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
